name: Superchunk
label: Matador
lede: A Kinko's night-shift grudge, a record label run out of a bedroom and thirty-odd years of the fastest, happiest-sounding frustration in Chapel Hill.

eras.title: Chunk, from a phonebook typo
eras.text: Mac McCaughan and Laura Ballance started a band and a record label in the same Chapel Hill summer. The band got its name from a misprint, the label got its name from a road sign, and the first real single got its name from a lazy co-worker.

years.h: Chunk forms in Chapel Hill, named for a phonebook misprint
years.p: Mac McCaughan, Laura Ballance, drummer Chuck Garrison and guitarist Jack McCook start a band called Chunk. The name came from Garrison's name misspelled in the phonebook.

years.h: McCaughan and Ballance start Merge Records in Ballance's bedroom
years.p: Fired up by a visit to Sub Pop's Seattle office, Mac McCaughan and Laura Ballance start Merge to put out 7-inches by their band and friends. Ballance named it after merge signs she saw driving through Colorado.
years.xp:
Merge started tiny: 7-inch singles only, packed and shipped from Ballance's bedroom. McCaughan's contacts from his job at Schoolkids Records helped them find distributors.

The label would outgrow the band's wildest hopes. In 2010 Merge had a Billboard No. 1 with [[Arcade Fire|52074ba6-e495-4ef3-9bb4-0703888a9f68]]'s The Suburbs, which went on to win the Grammy for Album of the Year.

years.h: Chunk becomes Superchunk to dodge a New York jazz band
years.p: After one single as Chunk, the band learns a New York jazz group already has the name. Adding Super settles it.

years.h: Slack Motherfucker, a song about a lazy Kinko's co-worker
years.p: Superchunk's first single under the new name comes out on Merge in a 1,000-copy pressing that sells out fast. Mac McCaughan wrote it about a slacker on his night shift at the Kinko's on Franklin Street.
years.xp:
Recorded January 18–19, 1990 at Duck Kee Studios in Raleigh, with Night Creatures on the B-side. College stations played it after midnight to stay clear of obscenity rules.

Drummer [[Chuck Garrison|e2cdcbfe-3f33-4acf-a168-b11979e8d72f]] has claimed the song was about him. McCaughan says it was the Kinko's guy. Laura Ballance later said she'd be happy never to hear it again, and the band dropped it from sets for a while in the 1990s before bringing it back.

years.h: Superchunk, the debut album, on Matador
years.p: Superchunk's first album comes out on Matador Records, then a young New York label run by Chris Lombardi. It includes Slack Motherfucker and gets the band strong reviews.

years.h: Jack McCook leaves; Jim Wilbur joins on guitar
years.p: Guitarist Jack McCook departs and Connecticut-born [[Jim Wilbur|15cf0928-cc87-4d5b-bb76-e0aa68528cad]], a Fairfield University graduate, takes over rhythm guitar. He is still in the band.

eras.title: Albini, Wurster and the Atlantic problem
eras.text: Superchunk made two Matador albums in two years, swapped drummers and got faster and tighter on the road with Rocket from the Crypt and Polvo. Then Matador signed a distribution deal with Atlantic, and the band walked.

years.src: Wikipedia: No Pocky for Kitty · Wikipedia: Superchunk
years.h: No Pocky for Kitty, recorded by Steve Albini in three days
years.p: Superchunk cut its second album April 21–23, 1991 at Chicago Recording Company with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]. The sleeve credits him as Laura, who sat in the right chair.
years.xp:
Pocky is a Japanese snack stick. The album runs about 33 minutes and includes Skip Steps 1 & 3, Cast Iron and Throwing Things. Chuck Garrison played drums on it but left weeks before it came out.

Merge reissued it in 1999 when Superchunk took back its Matador catalog.

years.h: Chuck Garrison out, Jon Wurster in on drums
years.p: Drummer Chuck Garrison quits weeks before No Pocky for Kitty is released. [[Jon Wurster|feab5f8f-f5ac-4e63-92a8-466dde483f8c]], from Raleigh band [[The Accelerators|abbf1897-7a1f-4e33-9a9f-612cedf550a9]], joins in October 1991 and stays 31 years.

years.h: Tossing Seeds, Merge's first full-length CD
years.p: The singles collection Tossing Seeds (Singles 89–91), catalog MRG020, is the first CD Merge ever releases. It puts Slack Motherfucker in front of a much bigger audience.

years.h: On the Mouth, produced by Rocket from the Crypt's John Reis
years.p: Recorded in a week in September 1992 at West Beach Studios with [[John Reis|626e7b64-3035-4f58-92a6-49790f600e30]], the album has Jon Wurster's first recordings with Superchunk. Precision Auto was later covered by [[Jimmy Eat World|bbc5b66b-d037-4f26-aecf-0b129e7f876a]].
years.xp: Mac McCaughan said the band thought it was soaking up Rocket from the Crypt, [[Drive Like Jehu|608c9da7-d3ef-4661-828b-24bb6ae20cd6]] and Polvo from touring together, but the result just sounds like a Superchunk record. The song called On the Mouth isn't on On the Mouth: it's a B-side of the Mower single.

years.h: Superchunk quits Matador over the Atlantic deal
years.p: When Matador Records signed a distribution deal with Atlantic Records in 1993, Superchunk left, even though they would not have had to put Atlantic's logo on their records.
years.xp:
From then on Superchunk released everything on Merge, the label McCaughan and Laura Ballance ran themselves. Matador went on to partner with Capitol in 1996 and bought that stake back in 1999.

Leaving turned out to be good for both sides: Merge became one of the biggest independent labels in America.

eras.title: Everything on Merge
eras.text: The first Merge album was written in the wreckage of McCaughan and Ballance's relationship, and the band kept playing it every night. Then came the widest-reaching records of the decade, Lollapalooza, strings, vibraphones and a party for the label's tenth birthday.

q: Touring for Foolish was so hard.
years.h: Foolish, made after Mac and Laura broke up
years.p: Superchunk's first Merge album, recorded at Pachyderm Studios in Minnesota with Brian Paulson, came right after Mac McCaughan and Laura Ballance's romantic split. Ballance painted the cover, with herself as model.
years.xp:
Ballance said playing the songs live meant listening to the words every night and feeling mute. She still rates it her third favorite Superchunk album.

Her cover was an unpracticed homage to an [[American Music Club|5837d14e-4d18-49cf-a759-e5818714bce4]] sleeve, with a dead rabbit added after she watched Michael Moore's Pets or Meat. The Driveway to Driveway video parodies The Philadelphia Story.

years.h: Here's Where the Strings Come In and Hyper Enough
years.p: Recorded at Fort Apache Studios in Boston, the album gives Superchunk a minor hit with the single Hyper Enough and its video. The band tours the world and plays Lollapalooza.
play: Here's Where the Strings Come In

years.h: Indoor Living brings in piano, organ and vibraphone
years.p: After a short break and an Australian tour, Superchunk records in Bloomington, Indiana with co-producer John Plymale. It is the band's most adventurous record so far.

years.h: Come Pick Me Up, with Jim O'Rourke at Electrical Audio
years.p: Superchunk's seventh album is recorded at [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]'s Electrical Audio in Chicago with [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] producing, pushing further the wider sound that began on Foolish.

years.h: Merge turns ten at the Cat's Cradle
years.p: Superchunk plays the Cat's Cradle in Carrboro for the label's tenth anniversary. The set later comes out as The Clambakes Series Vol. 3 in 2004.

eras.title: Slowing down, never stopping
eras.text: After Here's to Shutting Up, Superchunk stopped making albums but never broke up. The band scored a silent Japanese film, cut a single with a cartoon meatball, played pool parties and Coachella, and let Merge become a phenomenon.

years.h: Here's to Shutting Up starts the long pause
years.p: Superchunk's eighth album is the last for nine years. The band moves to occasional shows, many at the Cat's Cradle.

years.h: A live score for A Page of Madness at the Castro Theatre
years.p: At the San Francisco International Film Festival, Superchunk plays its own score to Teinosuke Kinugasa's 1926 silent film. It's released as The Clambakes Series Vol. 2, 2,500 copies.

years.h: Headlining The Daily Show's tenth birthday at Irving Plaza
years.p: Superchunk tops the bill at Irving Plaza in New York, with Clem Snide and Daily Show correspondents doing stand-up. Jon Wurster also drums with [[The Mountain Goats|9639cd52-c351-4a17-9797-58880e95a7ef]] that night for the first time.

years.h: Misfits and Mistakes, sung by Aqua Teen Hunger Force's Meatwad
years.p: A hidden track on the Aqua Teen Hunger Force movie soundtrack becomes a 7-inch: Superchunk's version on one side, the cartoon meatball Meatwad singing on the other.

years.h: First free show at Brooklyn's McCarren Park Pool
years.p: Superchunk headlines the first of the Pool Parties shows in an empty Brooklyn swimming pool. Around then they also cover [[Destiny's Child|a796b92e-c137-4895-9c89-10f900617a4f]]'s Say My Name for a compilation.

years.h: Coachella, alongside Yeah Yeah Yeahs and the Killers
years.p: Superchunk plays the festival in Indio, California, around the release of Leaves in the Gutter, its first new CD in seven years.

years.h: Our Noise tells the Merge story as the label turns 20
years.p: Mac McCaughan and Laura Ballance write the label history with John Cook. Merge celebrates with a six-day festival in Chapel Hill and Carrboro with more than 40 acts.

eras.title: Back at full speed
eras.text: Nine years after the last album, Superchunk came back sounding like it hadn't aged. The band lost Laura Ballance from the road to a hearing condition, kept going with a stand-in, and got angrier as the country did.

years.h: Majesty Shredding ends a nine-year wait
years.p: Superchunk's ninth album, recorded in Durham with Scott Solter, reaches No. 85 on the Billboard 200. Rolling Stone names it one of the 30 best albums of 2010.
years.xp: The New York Times' Jon Caramanica said the band had recaptured its bright, punkish power pop with no apparent effort. [[John Darnielle|dbd4a850-1276-4aac-8d29-b43e6a186b6b]] of the Mountain Goats guests. Metacritic scored it 83.

years.h: Jeff Mangum picks Superchunk for his ATP
years.p: [[Neutral Milk Hotel|a506f761-2c22-4b2f-8a94-bd748c2c8f75]]'s [[Jeff Mangum|6a7b9d5e-a863-4a90-a056-77942e9f43de]], a Merge artist, invites Superchunk to the All Tomorrow's Parties festival he curates in Minehead, England.

years.h: I Hate Music, Superchunk's tenth album
years.p: The band's tenth record follows Majesty Shredding and goes on the road to North America, Australia and the UK.

years.h: Laura Ballance stops touring because of hyperacusis
years.p: Ballance announces on the band's site that worsening hyperacusis, an extreme sensitivity to sound, keeps her off the tour. [[Jason Narducy|82dafda1-1848-4068-b78b-487fbb4573ae]] of [[Bob Mould|d7f5305a-15fc-4af4-a61b-f6f45510cc8f]]'s band plays bass live. She stays in the band.

years.h: Chuck Garrison returns for one Slack Motherfucker
years.p: At the end of a Scharpling & Wurster live show in Durham, the original drummer comes back to play the first single. Jon Wurster sings it in character as Philly Boy Roy.

years.h: What a Time to Be Alive, album eleven
years.p: Superchunk's eleventh album, announced in November 2017, arrives four and a half years after I Hate Music.

eras.title: Director of Percussive Research, retired
eras.text: The drummer who played on nearly everything left with a joke job title and a straight answer. A new drummer took over within a week, and Laura Ballance stepped away from the label she had co-founded.

years.h: Acoustic Foolish for Merge's 30th
years.p: Superchunk re-records its 1994 breakup album unplugged as part of the label's 30th-anniversary releases.

years.h: Wild Loneliness, Superchunk's twelfth
years.p: Superchunk's twelfth full-length is Jon Wurster's last album with the band.

q: My heart just isn't in it anymore.
years.h: Jon Wurster quits after 31 years
years.p: Wurster announces he is stepping back from his role as Director of Percussive Research at Superchunk Industries. The date is the 30th anniversary of On the Mouth, his first album with the band.
years.xp: Wurster posted the news on Instagram, wished the band well and said he'd be around for special occasions. He also plays with [[The Mountain Goats|9639cd52-c351-4a17-9797-58880e95a7ef]] and [[Bob Mould|d7f5305a-15fc-4af4-a61b-f6f45510cc8f]] and co-hosts The Best Show with Tom Scharpling.

years.h: Laura King debuts at a Carolina Hurricanes fan fest
years.p: One week after Wurster's exit, new drummer Laura King plays her first Superchunk show at the NHL team's Fan Fest in Raleigh.

years.h: Laura Ballance leaves Merge as Secretly Group buys in
years.p: Secretly Group takes a 50% stake in Merge. Co-founder Laura Ballance departs after more than 35 years; Mac McCaughan stays as president.

years.h: Songs in the Key of Yikes, album thirteen
years.p: Superchunk releases its thirteenth studio album on Merge, the first with Laura King on drums.
